subject: Dedicated capacity: burst seeding forecast & session-lifecycle probe
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@horizonai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Dan Rivera <dan.rivera@horizonai.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing inquiry — expected bursts and session mix

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Horizon AI is excited about Redwood's runtime. We're evaluating a reserved fleet for our recommendation and summarization surfaces. Before we schedule a technical kickoff, can you share the pre-sales sizing checklist or questionnaire you use to estimate dedicated capacity?

Quick context:
- Primary workload: conversational recommendations (multi-turn) + on-demand summaries of long docs.
- Expected pilot window: 1–2 weeks, then production commit if numbers match.
- Traffic profile (rough): avg 140 requests/min, peak bursts up to ~1,400 reqs/min for 5–10 minute windows; ~25% of requests are multi-turn sessions (avg 4 messages), remainder are single-turn summaries.
- Token profile: average prompt 350 tokens, average model-generated tokens 450 tokens; some summaries spike to 4k tokens.
- Latency SLO: 300ms p50, 900ms p95 for short responses; we can accept higher for very long summaries.

I've attached a small traffic sample and a handful of real response examples to help with sizing. Can you confirm what additional fields you need (e.g., session TTL, concurrency per user, retry/backoff behavior) and a rough committed capacity estimate for the pilot? Also include what GPU SKUs you typically propose for this profile.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Horizon AI
laura.chen@horizonai.com
[Attachment: horizon_traffic_sample.csv (csv)]
[Attachment: horizon_response_examples.jsonl (jsonl)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@horizonai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing inquiry — expected bursts and session mix

Hi Laura — thanks for the context and attachments, this is exactly the kind of sample we need. I've copied Marissa (solutions) to help with the pilot scoping and cost ballpark.

Attached is our lightweight dedicated sizing questionnaire — it focuses on the fields that materially change fleet footprint and GPU selection. Can you fill what you can and return? Below are the high-impact items we use to generate a pilot commitment and a conservative production footprint: 

High-impact sizing inputs (please provide if available):
- Peak burst magnitude (requests/min) and typical burst duration (minutes)
- Fraction of requests that are multi-turn sessions and average turns per session
- Average prompt tokens and average generated tokens (separately for short responses vs long summaries)
- % of requests that require context window >2k tokens (e.g., long-document summarization)
- Desired p50/p95 latency SLOs and acceptable p99 for bursts
- Session lifetime (how long KV cache is held in memory per active session)
- Parallelism per request (do requests fan out to multiple calls?)
- Expected concurrency growth pattern over 12 weeks post-commit
- Typical payload sizes and whether you use streaming responses
- Any regional placement requirements or data residency constraints

We typically map workloads like yours to two candidate SKUs depending on the summary tail:
1) A100/RTX8000-class (higher memory): recommended if >5% of production requests require >2k-token context or frequent 4k summarization.
2) H100 + quantized execution (higher throughput): recommended if most requests are short (<1k tokens) and you prioritize throughput/cost.

Pilot options we recommend:
- Canary pilot: reserved slice (10–15% of projected production concurrency) for 1 week with traffic replay + live shadowing.
- Spike soak: brief reserved burst capacity to validate autoscale and batching parameters.

Next steps:
1) Fill the attached questionnaire and send sample payloads (we'll use them to run a micro-benchmark).
2) Marissa will propose a pilot sizing and a high-level cost band.

I'll attach the questionnaire now.

Best,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-questionnaire.pdf (pdf)]

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@horizonai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing inquiry — expected bursts and session mix

Thanks Rishi — attached is our quick pass at the questionnaire and the traffic sample you requested. I filled the high-impact fields where we had clear telemetry; items marked TBD are things we can surface during the kickoff. Short answers here:

- Peak burst: 1,400 reqs/min, bursts typically 6–9 minutes.
- Multi-turn sessions: 25% of traffic, average 3.8 turns, session TTL 18 minutes.
- Prompt tokens: short requests 220 avg, summaries 1,100 avg; generated tokens: short 280 avg, summaries vary 1k–4k (top 1% near 4k).
- % >2k context: ~8% (primarily doc summarization).
- Latency SLO: target p50 300ms, p95 850ms, acceptable p99 2s (for long summaries).
- Concurrency growth: pilot -> +30% in 6 weeks if initial metrics look good.
- Streaming: yes for summaries.

Can you provide a rough committed capacity estimate for a 1-week pilot and a conservative production footprint (monthly commit)? Also please include what observability we'll have in the Console for token-level cost and per-route latency.

Attaching the completed questionnaire and a condensed payload sample.

Best,
Laura

--
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Horizon AI
[Attachment: horizon_questionnaire_filled.csv (csv)]
[Attachment: horizon_payload_samples.jsonl (jsonl)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@horizonai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Jul 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing inquiry — expected bursts and session mix

Hi Laura — great detail, this is very helpful. I'll own the pilot sizing and cost band. Quick notes and proposed next steps: 

1) Pilot sizing (rough):
- Recommend a reserved slice sized for sustained concurrency of ~350 concurrent inferences with a 4x headroom for bursts (we typically map your burst shape to autoscale + short reserved burst buffers).
- Suggested GPU mix for pilot: 2x H100 (quantized path for throughput) + 1x A100 slice pinned for long-context summaries during pilot windows.
- This maps to an estimated pilot commit of ~48 GPU-hours/day over a 7-day window (ballpark).

2) Production footprint (conservative monthly commit):
- If traffic scales per your growth plan, conservative commit: 12–16 H100-equivalent GPUs (mixed with 4 A100-class nodes for long-context workloads).

3) Observability & Console:
- You'll get per-route latency/tokens, token-level cost breakdowns, rollout traces, and a default eval set for quality monitoring. Streaming responses are instrumented; you can correlate token emission time to backend latency.

4) Next ops steps:
- Schedule a technical kickoff this week for payload replay and a micro-benchmark run. Suggested slots: Tue 10:00–11:30 PT or Wed 14:00–15:30 PT.
- We'll provision the pilot slice once the commercial terms are agreed (I'll send a HubSpot deal link and a draft SOW).

5) Ask for you: please share any hard SLOs for p99 or retention/compliance needs (KMS/HSM) we should account for in the Private deployment option.

I'll follow up with a short cost band and a draft pilot SOW (HubSpot: HZN-2028-007). Are you available for the Tue slot?

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
